doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His father the musician, opera and records, Italian at home
summary: His father taught every instrument and knew the operas; the music store brought in jazz records, and the family spoke Italian at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Your father was a professional musician?
He played all instruments and taught all instruments.
He came from Italy as a musician?
Do you know anything about his training in Italy, how he became a musician?

He knew every aria from every opera. He studied – I was a legit performer myself. When they call me a jazz drummer, I smile, because I was brought up with the opera – all the opera [?], and classical music. Of course, Dad having a music store, I got all the records – the jazz records that came in from Louis Armstrong, Benny Goodman, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Lionel Hampton, Cab Calloway. I knew all those records when I was a kid.
Francine said earlier that you only spoke Italian when you were a bambino. So Italian was spoken in the house?

Yeah, we spoke Italian all the time, because my parents didn’t understand English too much, so we spoke Italian. I spoke very fluently when I was a kid, but now I forgot it all, because after being on the road 50 years – or 70 years now – if I don’t talk to anybody, you lose it. But I still know all the cuss words.
